title: Console text can initiate plugin-failure recovery without source identity
description: The main WebView callback routes a console message to client-plugin failure handling based on its text prefix and does not check sourceId or emitting frame. That path can schedule rollback/quarantine for a uniquely matching plugin. Whether preview subframes can deliver such a message to the callback on supported WebView versions remains unresolved.
claimed_root_cause: Automatic plugin recovery trusts a reserved console prefix without binding the message to the trusted engine page or frame.

trace.description: The callback receives a ConsoleMessage and reads its text.
A matching message string enters the client plugin failure path without inspecting sourceId.
The recovery path uses failed IDs to select plugin entries for possible quarantine.

evidence.description: Client-failure routing is based on the message prefix.
The handler parses failed IDs from the console text.
The recovery path obtains the plugin patch and processes the parsed IDs.

blockers: Android WebView delivery of scriptable preview-frame console messages to this callback is not established by checked-in source.
The practical recovery effect also depends on a unique current plugin match and the recovery gates; no runtime message was delivered.

validation_plan.local: In an approved isolated Android/WebView fixture, load only a dummy untrusted preview frame and emit the reserved failure prefix with a synthetic plugin ID. Record whether the native callback receives it and whether only the dummy candidate reaches the recovery decision; do not alter real plugin state.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the Android owner check supported WebView versions with a disposable app/profile and confirm whether preview subframes can invoke this callback and trigger the gated recovery path.
